key_insight: FOCUS shows retinal AI models do not generalize uniformly: the best performer depends on the task, dataset, and evaluation criterion.
clinical_relevance: For safer retinal AI deployment, clinicians and developers should look beyond single-dataset accuracy and assess robustness, calibration, subgroup fairness, and image-quality sensitivity.
method: Built FOCUS, a cross-dataset benchmark for fundus imaging across 10 public datasets.
Harmonized binary DR, referable DR, and glaucomatous optic neuropathy tasks.
Compared vision-only encoders, vision-language dual encoders, and multimodal LLMs under shift, including calibration and subgroup analysis.
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 532 base model configurations and 228 LoRA-adapted MLLM configurations, finding no single model family consistently best across all settings.
watch_item: Improving in-domain performance did not reliably translate to external datasets, especially for calibration, so benchmark gains may not reflect real-world reliability.
paper_title: FOCUS: Benchmarking Retinal Model Generalization from Foundation Vision Encoders to Multimodal LLMs
